intro.data: A real inverse works both ways. Start from the packed form, Decode it, then Encode again — you should return to the packed form unchanged.
intro.alchemy: A real inverse works both ways. Start from the dust, Cast it, then Grind again — you should return to the dust unchanged.
intro.spellcraft: A real inverse works both ways. Start from the glyph, Read it, then Etch again — you should return to the glyph unchanged.
intro.abstract: A real inverse works both ways. Start from B, apply g, then f — you should return to B unchanged.

goal.data: Wire the start through Decode and then Encode, returning to the packed form.
goal.alchemy: Wire the start through Cast and then Grind, returning to the dust.
goal.spellcraft: Wire the start through Read and then Etch, returning to the glyph.
goal.abstract: Wire the start through g and then f, returning to B.

afterSuccess.data: The round trip the other way also returned home: f ∘ g = id_B. Since both round trips are the identity, Encode and Decode are inverses — an isomorphism.
afterSuccess.alchemy: The round trip the other way also returned home: f ∘ g = id_B. Since both round trips are the identity, Grind and Cast are inverses — an isomorphism.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The round trip the other way also returned home: f ∘ g = id_B. Since both round trips are the identity, Etch and Read are inverses — an isomorphism.
afterSuccess.abstract: The other round trip also returned home: f ∘ g = id_B. With both round trips identities, f and g are inverses — an isomorphism.

reveal.summary: An isomorphism is a morphism f with an inverse g such that g ∘ f = id_A and f ∘ g = id_B. The two objects are then interchangeable.
reveal.moreFormal: If f : A → B has a two-sided inverse g (both composites are identities), f is an isomorphism and we write A ≅ B. The inverse, when it exists, is unique.
